articles.title: Pete Hegseth’s Pentagon: A list of controversies that define his tenure
articles.summary: The defence secretary faces renewed scrutiny after a Republican senator called for his removal from the US cabinet.
articles.body:
United States Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth is facing increased scrutiny over his leadership of the Pentagon, with some of the criticism coming from within his own party.

On Wednesday, Republican Senator Thom Tillis urged President Donald Trump to replace Hegseth, accusing the defence secretary of creating a “leadership void” at the top of the US military.

“I have never witnessed more inept management of the brave men and women who serve our country,” Tillis said. “He is intimidated by competence.”

Tillis’s comments came after the resignation of Army Secretary Dan Driscoll on Monday, the latest high-ranking official to leave the Pentagon amid reported tensions with Hegseth.

Driscoll’s departure followed a series of firings, forced retirements and blocked promotions among senior military leaders, causing concern about the stability of the Pentagon’s leadership.

Hegseth, a former Fox News host and Army National Guard veteran, was confirmed as defence secretary in January 2025 after a contentious Senate vote .

Since taking office, he has pursued an aggressive effort to reshape the military, emphasising lethality and what he calls the “warrior ethos” . But senior officials argue that his approach has produced instability and prioritised cultural battles over military readiness .

His tenure has also been plagued by a series of controversies. Here are some of the notable ones so far:

The first major controversy of Hegseth’s tenure came in March 2025, just two months after his appointment.

A member of the Trump administration had inadvertently included Jeffrey Goldberg, the editor-in-chief of The Atlantic magazine, in a private chat on the messaging app Signal , where officials were discussing an impending attack on Yemen.

Hegseth featured prominently in the discussion. His messages included details about the timing of aircraft launches and strikes.

But Hegseth insisted that no “war plans” had been shared across the platform. Experts, however, disputed that assertion, noting that details about an upcoming military operation are typically classified.

The military prohibits the use of third-party platforms for operational security, and an inspector general’s report later indicated any leak from the Signal chat could have put service members in harm’s way.

Media reports also emerged indicating that Hegseth had been involved in a second Signal chat with his wife, brother and personal lawyer that also included sensitive military information .

Hegseth faced no formal punishment for the incidents.

Hegseth’s Pentagon has undergone a sweeping turnover of senior military and civilian officials.

Shortly after Hegseth assumed his role, several top military leaders were fired, including Navy Admiral Lisa Franchetti, Coastguard Commandant Linda Fagan and Charles Q Brown, the head of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

Both Fagan and Franchetti were the first women to serve in their roles. In a statement explaining Fagan’s termination, the Trump administration cited “leadership deficiencies” and an “excessive focus” on diversity.

Other officials have left or chosen an early retirement. They include figures like Navy Admiral Alvin Holsey, who faced criticism for his participation in the military’s boat strike campaign in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific Ocean under Hegseth.

The departures have continued into 2026, with Army Secretary Daniel Driscoll leaving his post on Wednesday.

Hegseth has taken the step of removing dozens of names from top military promotion lists, a rare move for a Pentagon chief.

Normally, candidates are identified by selection boards in the various branches of the military to be top officers. The process is supposed to be apolitical.

But Hegseth has reportedly knocked as many as 80 names off promotion lists for top military offices, including those expected to be elevated to one- or two-star generals.

Critics have questioned whether Hegseth has the authority to block promotions. Many have also noted that women and Black officers are disproportionately among those denied top-tier advancement.

Under Hegseth, the Pentagon has developed an increasingly adversarial relationship with journalists.

His department has restricted reporter access to the Pentagon press office, and in September 2025, unveiled a new policy requiring journalists to sign a pledge that would restrict their news gathering or else lose their media credentials .

That policy was blocked in March, with a district court ruling it ran afoul of the First Amendment’s free speech protections.

But further incidents have continued to raise concern about the press freedoms at the Pentagon. Last month, three members of the Stars and Stripes newspaper filed a lawsuit against the Defense Department for censorship , after they were fired for speaking out about editorial independence.

Hegseth, meanwhile, has publicly attacked the media, describing some coverage as “unpatriotic”.

Hegseth has made “lethality” a central tenet of the US military, a philosophy that has come under scrutiny during overseas military operations.

He has also pledged to jettison what he calls “stupid rules of engagement” that limit justifiable military action.

Since September 2, 2025, the US military has carried out a series of boat strikes in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific Ocean, on the premise of protecting the US from “narco-terrorists”.

But the identities of those killed remain largely a mystery, and no public evidence has been presented against them. Legal experts have called the campaign a series of extrajudicial killings, with the victims given no opportunity to plead their case.

Some families in Colombia, Trinidad, Ecuador and elsewhere fear those killed are innocent fishermen. So far, the death toll from the boat-strike campaign has reached 227, with the latest strikes taking place in August.

In at least one case, Hegseth reportedly ordered a “double-tap” attack to kill the survivors from an initial boat strike.

Hegseth, however, denied acting unlawfully, labelling coverage of the “double-tap” as “fabricated, inflammatory, and derogatory reporting”.

He also framed the lethal boat strikes as a corrective to policies under Trump’s predecessor, Joe Biden. “Biden coddled terrorists, we kill them,” Hegseth wrote.

Since February, the US has also been embroiled in a war on Iran that has raised similar use-of-force concerns. Hegseth has boasted that he unleashed the US military to use “maximum authorities on the battlefield” against Iran — a statement commonly understood to mean a loosening of the combat rules meant to protect civilians.

Those comments have drawn criticism after the US Tomahawk missile struck an Iranian elementary school on the first day of the war, killing an estimated 170 people, mostly children.

This week, Iranian officials also accused the US of hitting a civilian wedding in the city of Kuhestak, killing at least five people and wounding more than 60.

Questions about use of military resources

Under Hegseth, the Pentagon has requested a record $1.5 trillion from Congress for its defence budget in fiscal year 2027. Much of that proposal comes in the form of discretionary funding.

The Pentagon has framed the sum as a “generational investment”. But critics have argued that the military is effectively asking for a blank cheque, without accounting for the 42-percent increase in its budget.

The Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, a think tank, went so far as to call the sum “unhinged”.

Some of that sum is likely aimed at helping to offset the costs of the US-Israel war on Iran.

In July, Hegseth testified to the Senate Appropriations Committee that $37.5bn had been spent on the war so far. The amount is higher than the $25bn estimate the Defense Department gave in April.

Reports have emerged that US stockpiles of certain munitions are also low, raising concerns about the US strategy against Iran and its ability to defend against other threats.

Under Hegseth and Trump, the US military has embarked on several military campaigns that appear to violate international law.

On January 3, for instance, the US military launched an operation to abduct Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, transporting him to New York to face trial.

While the Trump administration has called the operation a domestic law enforcement action, critics have framed it as a violation of a foreign country’s sovereignty.

The US and Israel also launched the initial attacks that kicked off the ongoing war on Iran. While the Trump administration has argued that Iran posed an imminent threat, prominent legal experts have called the conflict an unprovoked war of choice.

As the war stretches into its seventh month, Hegseth has faced criticism for not having a clear exit strategy. The conflict has also contributed to instability and violence across the Middle East, as well as a surge in oil prices .

Hegseth has rejected what he calls “wokeness” in the US military.

His tenure has seen a rollback of policies designed, or perceived, to promote diversity in the ranks. Under orders from Trump, he has also overseen the expulsion of transgender service members from the military.

Hegseth has also embraced a return to more traditional ideas of masculinity. That has included plans for testosterone testing among troops over 30 and new grooming standards under the slogan “No More Beardos”.

Hegseth has also drawn scrutiny for blurring the separation of church and state. He has been known to lead a regular Christian prayer service at the Pentagon and has framed some of the military’s actions in religious terms.

articles.title: Ghana tightens gold exports in push to keep more value at home
articles.summary: The move is part of a broader effort to develop Ghana’s gold industry beyond raw exports.
articles.body:
Accra, Ghana – Ghana is requiring certain gold exporters to refine gold dore locally before it can be shipped abroad, in a move aimed at keeping more of the value generated by the country’s gold industry at home.

Effective September 1, the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) barred Self-Financing Aggregators (SFAs) from exporting gold dore purchased under arrangements with approved offtakers unless it is first refined in Ghana.

Dore is semi-refined gold that requires further processing before it can be turned into bullion.

The directive, issued by GoldBod’s Compliance Directorate on August 24, implements the Ghana Gold Board Act, 2025 (Act 1140), which established GoldBod as the authority overseeing the buying, selling, assaying, refining and export of gold in Ghana.

For Clement Edem Asare Morjah, chief executive of United Gold International Limited, a licensed SFA, the policy marks a significant change in how Ghana handles its most valuable natural resource.

“For the first time since independence, we have a government determined to make sure Ghana benefits from our biggest resource, gold,” he said.

Morjah said refining gold locally could allow Ghanaian companies to capture margins that have historically gone to overseas processors.

“In the entire value chain between refining and raw processed gold, the cost in between is a lot of margins. Historically, we have lost this to the outside world for decades. This is the first time deliberate government policy is trying to address this anomaly,” Morjah said.

But he added the short notice had created challenges for companies with existing contracts, which may now have to be amended.

GoldBod had required SFAs to amend existing offtake agreements by August 31. Export applications would only be processed after GoldBod confirms that the gold has been refined locally, applicable charges have been settled and other regulatory requirements have been met.

Prince Kwame Minkah, GoldBod’s media relations officer, said the policy was intended to ensure Ghana captured more of the economic benefits from its gold.

“Ghana is one of the top gold-producing countries in the world, so we need to truly maximise national benefits,” he said. “Value addition is key.”

He said the policy was consistent with President John Mahama’s vision that, by 2030, Ghana’s natural resources should be exported with a certain level of value addition.

“The value addition is what will culminate in the building of a gold industry in Ghana,” Minkah said.

Local refining, he added, could create jobs, reduce the amount of money paid overseas for processing and provide refined gold for industries such as jewellery manufacturing.

GoldBod also plans to develop a gold village modelled on Dubai’s Gold Souk, he said.

Ghana has four licensed gold refineries, including Gold Coast Refinery and Royal Ghana Gold Refinery.

Gold Coast Refinery, which opened in 2016, has a stated capacity of up to two tonnes a week, while Royal Ghana Gold Refinery, commissioned in August 2024, has a daily capacity of 400 kilogrammes (882 pounds).

GoldBod has supply agreements with both refineries. Under its agreement with Gold Coast Refinery, GoldBod supplies at least one metric tonne of gold a week.

Gold Coast Refinery is also in partnership with South Africa’s Rand Refinery.

Minkah said GoldBod was building what he described as “the largest refinery on the African continent” in Ghana.

Ghana produced nearly six million ounces, or about 185 tonnes, of gold in 2025, with small-scale mining accounting for about 3.1 million ounces (96 tonnes), up from 1.9 million ounces (59 tonnes) the previous year.

Gold export earnings reached about $20bn in 2025, nearly double the $10.3bn recorded in 2024, while total merchandise exports stood at about $31.1bn.

The surge has increased the government’s focus on bringing more of the gold value chain under domestic control.

George Darkwa, a gold and mineral expert, said the refining requirement was a positive development for the industry.

“It is a positive move that will enhance value retention and formalisation,” he said, urging foreign investors to support Ghana’s efforts to develop its domestic gold industry.

GoldBod said exporting, or attempting to export, unrefined dore in breach of the new requirements would violate licence conditions.

Possible sanctions include the refusal or suspension of export approvals, suspension or revocation of licences, administrative penalties and other enforcement measures.

The board said the directive was intended to strengthen regulation while retaining more domestic value through refining and other forms of value addition.

For Morjah, the benefits could eventually extend beyond the companies directly affected by the new rule.

Once refined, gold becomes bullion that can meet recognised standards, he said, making its quality and value more predictable.

“Give it time,” Morjah said. “Everybody will understand the benefit. When you’re doing business, you don’t only think about your individual benefit as a company. You must think about the body corporate as a nation.”

articles.title: In 1909, engineers built a hydroelectric plant in Arizona, where mule teams carried construction materials up mountains
articles.summary: US News: In the rugged mountains of central Arizona, building a hydroelectric plant in the early 20th century meant overcoming obstacles that modern constructi.
articles.body: In the rugged mountains of central Arizona, building a hydroelectric plant in the early 20th century meant overcoming obstacles that modern construction crews rarely face. In 1909, engineers completed the Childs Plant, part of the Childs-Irving Hydroelectric Project near the Verde River, harnessing the dramatic drop in elevation of Fossil Creek to generate electricity. The terrain was so difficult that mule teams had to carry construction materials up the mountains, forcing engineers to rethink how parts of the project could be built and connected. According to the Engineering and Technology History Wiki (ETHW), the project eventually became an important source of electricity for Arizona and was later recognised as an ASME Historic Mechanical Engineering Landmark. The Childs Plant used three Pelton-wheel generators and demonstrated how hydroelectric technology could be adapted to an exceptionally challenging landscape. What began as an ambitious engineering project ultimately helped supply the entire electric demand of Yavapai County.Arizona’s 1909 hydroelectric plant conquered rugged mountain terrainThe Childs-Irving Hydroelectric Project was built around the dramatic natural drop of Fossil Creek, which travels roughly 10 miles towards the Verde River while descending about 1,600 feet. That elevation difference offered engineers an opportunity to turn flowing water into electricity at a time when hydroelectric power was becoming increasingly important. The Childs Plant was completed in 1909 with three Pelton-wheel generators producing 9,000 horsepower, or about 6,700 kilowatts. The Irving Plant followed in 1916 with an Allis-Chalmers Francis turbine. ETHW notes that the remote, mountainous location created an extraordinary logistical challenge. Mule teams carried construction materials through the terrain, making conventional wooden transmission poles impractical and encouraging the engineers to use steel towers instead.Mule teams carried construction materials through Arizona’s mountainsThe construction story reveals just how different major engineering projects were before modern roads, heavy trucks and helicopters transformed remote construction. The Childs-Irving project occupied mountainous terrain where simply getting materials to the right location was itself an engineering problem. Mule teams carried construction materials up the mountains, according to ETHW’s account of the project. The difficulty influenced the design of the electrical transmission system, with engineers using steel towers instead of wooden poles. The project also required a seven-mile series of flumes to bring water from a dam below Fossil Spring towards the Irving Plant, before the water continued towards the Childs Plant’s penstocks. The system effectively turned the landscape’s natural elevation into a source of mechanical and electrical power.The Childs Plant once powered Yavapai CountyAlthough the Childs Plant would appear modest by modern standards, its impact was substantial for the Arizona communities it served. ETHW records that the Childs and Irving plants once supplied the entire electric requirements of Yavapai County. A 75-mile transmission line was later constructed in 1919 from Sycamore to Phoenix, carrying 2,000 kilowatts of power. By the middle of the 1920s, that line was delivering approximately 70% of all electricity used in Phoenix, which at the time had a population of about 44,000. The project therefore became more than an isolated mountain power station. It formed part of the growing electrical infrastructure that helped connect remote generating facilities with expanding Arizona communities and industries.Why Arizona’s 1909 hydroelectric project became an ASME landmarkThe Childs-Irving Hydroelectric Project was eventually recognised as ASME Historic Mechanical Engineering Landmark #13, designated on 10 April 1976. The Engineering and Technology History Wiki explains that ASME’s landmark programme recognises existing artefacts and systems representing significant achievements in mechanical engineering. The Childs-Irving project stands out because it combined hydroelectric machinery with an ingenious response to an exceptionally difficult environment. The Childs Plant’s three Pelton-wheel generators represented the technology of their era, while the project’s transmission system had to accommodate the practical realities of transporting equipment through mountainous country. More than a century after the Childs Plant was completed, its story remains a striking example of early hydroelectric engineering, when generating electricity could begin with little more than flowing water, ambitious engineers and mule teams carrying materials into the mountains.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: US continues to squeeze Cuban economy with new round of sanctions
articles.summary: Cuba announces new pro-market reforms amid threats of military attack from the Trump administration.
articles.body:
The United States has announced a new series of economic sanctions targeting Cuba, its latest step in a campaign to squeeze the island’s already fragile economy.

The US State Department said on Thursday that it was sanctioning several Cuban companies and 31-year-old Fidel Ernesto Castro, grandson of 95-year-old former leader Raul Castro.

“Cuba’s Communist regime elites preside over a failed state where ordinary Cubans go hungry,” US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a social media post on Thursday.

Since January, President Donald Trump has undertaken a heightened campaign to weaken Cuba’s government, in an effort to spur regime change.

Part of that campaign has been a series of escalating sanctions, as well as a de facto fuel blockade. Cuba had already been under a historic, decades-long US embargo that stretches back to the Cold War.

But Rubio argued that further actions were necessary to penalise Cuba’s leadership for decades of mismanagement and repression.

He further accused Cuba of seeking to “export subversive Marxist ideology to the United States and other states in the Western Hemisphere”, echoing Trump’s assertions that the island is a national security threat.

Since the start of the heightened pressure campaign in January, Cuba has taken steps to defuse the criticism.

In June, it passed its biggest free-market reforms in decades, with 176 new measures. It has also conducted prisoner releases as a “humanitarian and sovereign gesture”.

On Thursday, further reforms were announced, with 34 pages of legal changes designed to loosen regulation and state control in industries like tourism.

Under the new rules, private companies will be able to establish tour and travel agencies, separate from the Cuban government. They also will not have to contract employees through state agencies.

It will also become easier for some domestic investors to open foreign bank accounts.

But such steps have thus far done little to placate the Trump administration.

Since the start of the year, the US has repeatedly threatened Cuba with military intervention , and its sanction campaign has continued.

Critics warn that the sanctions, combined with the ongoing energy blockade, have pushed the country’s power grid and healthcare systems to the point of collapse.

Volker Turk , the high commissioner for human rights at the United Nations, stated in June that such restrictions were “directly harming Cubans” and called for their end.

“Children are dying because doctors lack access to essential medical supplies and medicines,” said Turk. “This is unacceptable.”

Rubio, on the other hand, has argued that Cuba’s government, a thorn in the side of Washington since the leftist revolution of 1959, is responsible for the island’s poor economic conditions.

Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez accused the US of fabricating threats as a pretext for pressuring the country, in an interview published in the state-run newspaper Gramma on Thursday.

“The truth is that Cuba does not threaten US national security or the US economy, nor does it wish to do so,” he said. “The accusation that Cuba allegedly sponsors terrorism actually reveals the US government’s lack of seriousness.”

In addition to targeting the Castro family, Thursday’s new sanctions cover two companies involved in Cuba’s nickel mining industry, two companies active in Cuba’s flagging energy sector, including an oil import company, and Banco Exterior de Cuba, a state-owned bank.

articles.title: WATCH: Bystanders, police lift Volkswagen off woman pinned underneath after dramatic e-bike crash
articles.summary: Body camera video captured strangers and officers lifting a Volkswagen Beetle off a trapped e-bike rider after a crash on a Prospect Park road.
articles.body: A group of strangers and police officers rushed to lift a Volkswagen Beetle off an injured e-bike rider after she became trapped beneath the car during a crash on a busy Pennsylvania road, dramatic body camera video shows. Local authorities said the 44-year-old woman suffered several broken bones in Monday morning's crash in Prospect Park but survived after roughly six bystanders joined officers to lift the vehicle and pull her to safety, FOX 29 reported. Prospect Park Police Chief Dave Madonna said the woman was riding an e-bike more than 20 mph, according to his estimate, without a helmet when she collided with the Volkswagen at an intersection along Route 420. "She was driving way too fast for that time of day, for the road she was traveling on," Madonna said, adding that he believed she had been trying to overtake vehicles while traveling to an appointment. RESCUERS FREE CLIMBER TRAPPED BENEATH 16,000-POUND BOULDER ON OREGON'S MOUNT HOOD IN COMPLEX OPERATION Surveillance and police body camera video shows bystanders rushing to the crash to help. About six people then work together to lift the car high enough to free the woman trapped underneath. "Got a yell to help, ran over. We lifted the Volkswagen Beetle up, pulled the girl out and pushed her to the ground so she wouldn't move, that's all," FedEx driver Carl Wise told the station. GOOD SAMARITAN IN SPIDER-MAN COSTUME HELPS MAN IN WHEELCHAIR CROSS BUSY INTERSECTION IN VIRAL MOMENT "I'm no hero. I'm just a guy doing a job, that's all," he added. Local business owner Chrissy Vollmer, who also responded, described what she saw. "All I saw were the lady's legs underneath the car, and she was just yelling, ‘Get this car off of me,’" Vollmer said. Madonna called the bystanders who helped rescue the woman "heroes" and later visited them to offer his thanks. ICE OFFICER HAILED AS HERO AFTER SAVING DRIVER INJURED IN MISSOURI CRASH He also raised concerns about what he described as an increase in e-bike crashes. "How many more tragedies do we have to see before some type of action is taken?" Madonna said. The woman was taken to Lankenau Hospital and underwent surgery for a broken collarbone and other injuries, FOX 29 reported. articles.title: 'Operation Economic Outcast': EU joins Donald Trump's campaign to squeeze Iran
articles.summary: Europe News: US treasury secretary Scott Bessent on Thursday said the European Union has thrown its weight behind Donald Trump's strong economic campaign against I.
articles.body: US treasury secretary Scott Bessent on Thursday said the European Union has thrown its weight behind Donald Trump's strong economic campaign against Iran, claiming the bloc has "officially joined" the US-led "Operation Economic Outcast"."The European Union has officially joined Operation Economic Outcast and we appreciate their strong and early stance," Bessent said in a statement on X.The announcement came as the EU signalled that it could support further economic measures against Tehran, while making clear that diplomatic efforts and de-escalation must continue alongside the pressure campaign."The United States stands firm with our allies in ensuring the murderous Iranian regime cannot exploit the global financial system to fund its nuclear ambitions, weapons programs, and terror proxies. The world is sending a clear message to the Iranian regime: We will not stop until every remaining financial lifeline has been severed," he added.The EU listed several areas of concern behind its position, including Iran's nuclear and ballistic missile programmes, its regional activities and its alleged support for Russia in the war in Ukraine."The European Union has consistently urged Iran to curb its nuclear programme, and its ballistic missile programme, refrain from destabilising activities in the region and in Europe, stop its military support for Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and cease the violence and repression against its own people," the EU said in a statement shared by Bessent.At the same time, Brussels stressed that economic pressure alone would not be enough to resolve the crisis. It said diplomacy remained essential for a peace settlement, restoration of regional stability and ensuring "full freedom of navigation and safe transit through the Strait of Hormuz".The Strait has emerged as a key flashpoint amid the conflict, with disruptions to shipping and energy flows raising concerns well beyond the region.The EU said it had already put in place broad sanctions designed to restrict Iran's ability to use international economic and financial systems to pursue activities that the bloc considers a threat to international security."It remains ready to take further measures, where necessary, to safeguard its security and interests, including freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz," the EU said.Brussels also linked any further economic action to efforts to bring Iran back to negotiations.The bloc welcomed moves aimed at pushing Tehran to end its destabilising activities and enter peace talks "with good faith", saying additional economic pressure through Operation Economic Outcast could form part of that approach."The EU will continue to work closely with the United States and other G7 and international partners to maintain pressure on Iran and contribute to de-escalation and regional stability," it said.What is Operation Economic OutcastWashington unveiled the operation last month as a broad financial campaign targeting Iran's economic lifelines. Bessent said the US treasury was seeking to isolate Tehran from international financial networks while targeting sources of revenue that Washington believes help sustain the Iranian government."The US Department of the Treasury has launched Operation Economic Outcast, an unprecedented campaign against the Islamic Republic of Iran and its neighbours," Bessent said when announcing the initiative."Our goal is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime," he said.As part of the campaign, the US said it had mapped networks allegedly being used by Iran to move oil and get around existing sanctions. Washington also widened the range of Iran-linked activities that could trigger sanctions, with digital assets, technology and shipping among the areas coming under greater scrutiny.Bessent had framed the campaign as a choice between economic isolation and reintegration into the global economy."Iran now faces a clear choice, with only two paths before them: complete global isolation and a subsistence economy, or a path to normalcy with the opportunity to rejoin the global economy," he had said.Pressure and diplomacyThe EU's position represents a balancing act: Closer coordination with Washington on economic pressure, while keeping diplomacy at the centre of its approach.By signalling its readiness to participate in additional measures, the bloc could add greater weight to the US effort to squeeze Tehran financially. But its emphasis on negotiations, de-escalation and freedom of navigation also underlines Europe's interest in preventing the economic campaign from further widening the conflict.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Argentina to sanction oil firms as Falklands dispute with UK heats up
articles.summary: Javier Milei reiterates his country's claim on the British overseas territory, saying the "winds of change" favour it.
articles.body:
Argentina's President, Javier Milei, has heightened tensions with the UK over the Falklands, warning he will impose economic sanctions on firms which exploit oil close to the British overseas territory.

In a national address, Milei said the "winds of change" favoured Argentina's claim to the islands, emboldened by signs the US might reconsider its stance of neutrality on the issue.

Milei said the Sea Lion oilfield, where a British and an Israeli firm are due to begin exploration work, was a "clear and present danger".

More than 40 years after the war over the territory, sovereignty of the archipelago in the south-west Atlantic Ocean remains hotly disputed between Britain and Argentina.

BBC News is seeking comment from the UK government on Milei's statement. It reiterated this week that Falkland islanders "are British with a right to determine their own future".

Milei announced his sanctions plan surrounded by his cabinet at the presidential palace, reiterating that the Falklands were "historically and legally" Argentinean.

Teslyn Barkman, a former member of the Falkland Islands Legislative Assembly, told the BBC that Milei's speech had "probably irked every single Falkland islander".

Speaking from the capital Stanley, she added that "we have a burgeoning economy for a small place... we will remain forever British".

The crux was a proposal to introduce a bill to parliament to impose sanctions on energy firms planning to begin oil exploration off the Falklands.

The Sea Lion oilfield , around 130 miles from the islands, contains an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil.

Two oil companies – Britain's Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum – are due to begin extracting oil in the Sea Lion oilfield off the Falklands coast within two years, something Milei said Argentina could not allow.

Rockhopper has described the field as containing "highly marketable crude".

In a video posted earlier this year, Navitas highlighted the work it is already carrying out in the Falklands including building a dock, a heliport and accommodation for oil workers.

The BBC has contacted the two companies for responses to Milei's latest comments.

"If we do not act swiftly in a few months, they will have the material capacity to access the oil that lies underneath our sea – something that has never happened before," Milei said.

It is not yet clear how or to what extent the sanctions will be imposed or tightened. In Argentina, a current law already allows for restrictions of activities of oil companies participating in projects considered unauthorised on the islands.

In a 2013 referendum, residents of the islands voted overwhelmingly to remain a British overseas territory - with 99.8% voting in favour and just three voting against.

When asked in an interview with GB News earlier on Thursday if the US would "come to the UK's aid" during a potential territorial dispute, Trump replied that Britain had "not been there to help me" with his country's war with Iran.

Trump's latest remarks come after he previously said the US could revise its neutral position on the islands' sovereignty if the UK failed to increase defence spending.

Milei also announced plans for a naval base in Tierra del Fuego in the south of Argentina, saying Trump and the US were "assessing their historical position in regard to the Falklands", which Argentina refers to as Las Malvinas.

"That is not empty words as they understand that Argentina is a reliable partner and a valuable ally for decades to come," he said , describing the UK as a nation "in decline".

"There are winds of change in the world that are favourable to our claim," Milei added.

Hours before Milei's speech, Sarah Rogers, a senior official in the US state department, posted a photo of herself with Milei alongside the caption: "Exciting things are happening in the Western Hemisphere."

Argentine forces landed on the Falklands to stake a territorial claim in 1982, sparking a 74-day war over the territory as a British military task force ejected them.

The conflict led to the deaths of 255 British military personnel, three islanders and 649 Argentine military personnel.

In a sign of the ongoing tensions between the two countries over the issue, Argentina players celebrated their victory over England in the World Cup by waving a banner in support of their country's territorial claim.

articles.title: Influencer boasts of 'not being jailed' after 'cracking skull' during CJP protest; police respond
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Opposition parties have targeted the BJP after a video surfaced in which self-styled influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj claimed that a phone cal.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Opposition parties have targeted the BJP after a video surfaced in which self-styled influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj claimed that a phone call from Delhi minister Kapil Mishra helped him avoid jail after he allegedly attacked the father of a student protester.Bhardwaj has been accused of assaulting Sanjay Kumar, the father of student activist Nishu Azad, during a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar.Also read: ‘Feel the power!’: Influencer flaunts kada in Instagram story after ‘cracking CJP protester’s skull’ at Jantar MantarIn the video, Bhardwaj appears to speak about the alleged attack and claims to have the backing of several political leaders, including Mishra, Union minister Chirag Paswan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi questioned why Bhardwaj was not jailed and asked whether he enjoyed political protection."I cracked the skull of Nishu's father. Do you know which section this crime attracts? Section 307. He needed 60 stitches. The man was being taken away in an ambulance in a serious condition. His daughter was standing outside the police station and saying that she would die by suicide if her father didn't get justice. But I was not even jailed. The world should know this. I was out and about through the night," Bhardwaj is heard saying in the video."I have the blessings of Hanuman. Secondly, Kapil Mishra is my elder brother. They say Kapil Mishra called and I was released. Chirag Paswan is my elder brother. How many leaders do you know? Do you know Modi ji? Modi ji is also my elder brother. I have everyone's support," he says.News agency PTI contacted Mishra and Paswan for their response but received no reply.Delhi Police rejects claims of serious injuryDelhi Police later rejected claims that Kumar had suffered a fractured skull or serious injuries.In a post on X, the office of the deputy commissioner of police, New Delhi, said Kumar had suffered a head injury from a kada, or bangle, worn by one of the men involved in a scuffle."On 23.06.2026, at Jantar Mantar, during the CJP protest, Sanjay Kumar (38), a resident of Ghaziabad, sustained a head injury by Kada worn by one of the alleged during a scuffle."He was medically examined by doctors of RML Hospital, and the injuries were opined to be simple in nature. The injuries were made by kada and not by any weapon. The misinformation regarding crack in skull is not supported by facts/ MLC and is completely baseless," the post said.Police said a case was registered at Parliament Street police station on Kumar's statement."They were detained from the site and during investigation, Suraj Kumar (24) and Swatantra Bhardwaj (21) were served notices as per law and were interrogated. Due legal action has been taken, and chargesheet would be filed before the competent court soon."Any allegation of undue influence or interference in the matter is factually incorrect and baseless. The matter has been dealt with strictly in accordance with law and procedures," it said.Around the time the police issued the statement, Bhardwaj posted a photograph of himself on Instagram showing his kada, with the caption "Feel the power!"Rahul Gandhi backs student protesterThe controversy has drawn support for Azad from opposition parties, including the Congress, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Trinamool Congress (TMC).Gandhi said the student was being targeted for raising her voice over the rights of her community and students."Nishu, there's no need to panic. I'm with you. It's clear that you're being targeted because you raise your voice for the rights of your community and students. Amit Shah's Delhi Police, on one hand, commits inhuman brutality against students. On the other hand, the criminal who smashed the head of a Dalit girl's father is roaming freely in the open."Tagging Prime Minister Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah, he asked, "Why does such a criminal have the protection of you and the people in your party? Will there be action now, or will you keep shielding someone?"Gandhi was responding to a post by Azad in which she said she hoped the opposition leader would help deliver justice."I will fight and I will win this battle," she wrote.Earlier, after Bhardwaj's video went viral, Azad had expressed concern about the safety of herself and her family."I'm worried about my and my family's safety, but I won't be scared -- I will continue my fight against injustice and casteism. @DelhiPolice is not taking any action, and we hope that all the opposition leaders will deliver justice to me, a daughter of the Dalit community," she wrote on X.Kejriwal, Mahua Moitra attack BJPAAP chief Arvind Kejriwal also shared Bhardwaj's video on X and attacked PM Modi."You absolutely must watch this video. Your blood will boil. Did heroes like Bhagat Singh sacrifice their lives for this, that one day the country would get a prime minister who would openly protect such thugs?" Kejriwal asked.TMC Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra questioned Home Minister Amit Shah over the allegations and said a movement demanding his resignation should continue."So shouldn't the movement for Amit Shah's resignation continue? Isn't he responsible? Sept 5 March was called off because 20 odd Delhi FIRs were recalled but isn't this also part of the brutality which will go unaccounted for?" Moitra asked.'I will be coming with my father'The CJP has demanded action against Bhardwaj and questioned why Delhi Police had not acted on what it described as an "open admission".The outfit said its members would reach Parliament Street police station at 10am on Friday to seek justice for Kumar and Azad.Responding to the announcement, Azad said, "I will be coming with my father."Kumar was attacked during the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in July, when his daughter was participating in and documenting the student agitation.CJP spokesperson Saurav Das alleged that Kumar's "skull was cracked open" and said the nature of the wound warranted an attempt-to-murder charge.He alleged that police had refused to add the charge to the FIR.Das said an attempt-to-murder charge would have led to Bhardwaj's immediate arrest because it is a cognisable and non-bailable offence.He alleged that deputy commissioner Sachin Sharma and Assistant Commissioner Ajay Sharma had refused the demand and asked the protesters to "go get a court order".Das also questioned whether Mishra should be named in the case over the alleged phone call."So tell us, why should (minister Kapil) Mishra not be made an accomplice in the FIR since he illegally interfered with the course of justice? Why should he not resign for protecting gang members and abusing his office? Does BJP's leadership support this?" Das wrote on X.Who is Swatantra Bhardwaj?Bhardwaj has a sizeable social media following, with 1.84 lakh users following his Instagram account. His profile describes him as a "Swatantra Sanatani Yodha".He has posted several videos targeting people participating in the CJP agitation.In a video posted during the July 20 protest, he called the protesters "terrorists" and "cockroaches" and demanded that "staunch sanatanis" like him be allowed to act as Delhi Police personnel for a day.The latest controversy has put renewed focus on the police handling of the assault case and on Bhardwaj's claims that he has political connections.Delhi Police has denied any undue influence or interference, saying the case has been handled according to law and that a chargesheet will be filed before the competent court.(With inputs from PTI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: NBA star Yao Ming saw elephants and rhinos killed for ivory and horns; he later became a leading wildlife conservation campaigner in China
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Yao Ming had spent years being watched by millions of people, but nothing in his basketball career prepared him for what he encountered in Africa. In .
articles.body: Yao Ming had spent years being watched by millions of people, but nothing in his basketball career prepared him for what he encountered in Africa. In August 2012, the former NBA star travelled through Kenya and South Africa to see the impact of the illegal wildlife trade firsthand. He watched elephants in the wild, then came across the remains of five elephants killed by poachers. Later, he saw a rhino that had suffered the same fate. The scenes gave a human face to statistics about ivory and rhino horn that could otherwise feel distant to consumers thousands of kilometres away. Yao also met conservationists, government officials and children whose education benefited from wildlife tourism. When he returned to China, he carried those experiences into a public campaign against the trade. His celebrity gave the message unusual reach, but it was the animals he had seen that gave him a personal reason to speak.What Yao saw in Africa turned a wildlife campaign into a deeply personal causeYao's journey in August 2012 lasted 12 days. It was not simply a wildlife tour. He was there to document the threats facing elephants and rhinos and to understand the people dealing with them on the ground.In Kenya, he saw elephants before encountering the remains of five that had been killed by poachers. In South Africa, he came across a rhino that had suffered the same fate. The contrast was difficult to ignore: living animals on one part of the journey, carcasses on another, with the demand for their body parts connecting the two.He also met children whose schooling benefited from income generated by wildlife tourism, as well as conservation workers and government officials involved in protecting animals from poachers.The material gathered during the trip was later used in a documentary project and in public service announcements aimed at Chinese audiences.Why many people misunderstood the ivory tradeThe campaign came at a time when elephant poaching had become a serious concern across parts of Africa. According to the African Wildlife Foundation, the information released with the campaign estimated that more than 25,000 elephants were being killed for ivory each year, with levels approaching those seen before the international ivory trade ban introduced in 1989.China was a particularly important part of the discussion because of its ivory market. Although international trade in ivory was prohibited, a one-off legal sale in 2008 had created a regulated market in China and Japan. Conservation groups said the system was being exploited to conceal illegal ivory.A survey commissioned in late 2012 offered another problem. Awareness of the poaching crisis did not necessarily match the scale of the trade.The survey, carried out in Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou among almost 1,000 people, found that more than half of those questioned did not believe elephant poaching was common. About a third thought ivory came from elephants that had died naturally. Only 33 per cent identified poaching for tusks as the reason elephants were being killed.Yet there was considerable support for government action. Ninety-four per cent of those surveyed agreed that the Chinese government should ban the ivory trade.Many buyers still believed rhino horn had special usesThe situation surrounding rhino horn had its own complications. A separate survey in the same three Chinese cities found that two-thirds of respondents did not know that rhino horn was obtained from poached animals. Almost half believed it could be legally bought through official shops.The findings also pointed to misconceptions about why people wanted the product. Traditional Chinese medicine had officially removed rhino horn from China's pharmacopeia in 1993, but demand had not disappeared. Some consumers continued to associate it with supposed medicinal or sexual properties.Rhino horn was also being treated by some buyers as an investment or used for ornamental carvings.According to the African Wildlife Foundation, South Africa had recorded 668 rhinos killed by poachers in 2012 alone, according to the campaign material. The figures illustrated how quickly the illegal trade had grown and why conservation organisations were trying to address not only poaching in Africa but demand in Asian markets.Why Yao Ming was the right voice for the campaignThe choice of Yao as the public face of the campaign was not accidental. He had already become involved in a high-profile effort to reduce the consumption of shark fin in China through WildAid.That earlier campaign gave conservation groups an example of what a recognisable Chinese celebrity could do when the message reached a mass audience.The organisations involved in the ivory and rhino campaign included WildAid, Save the Elephants, the African Wildlife Foundation and the Yao Ming Foundation. Their approach relied heavily on public education rather than presenting the issue solely as a distant conservation problem.Yao's role was particularly useful because he could speak directly to Chinese consumers in a way that international conservation organisations could not always replicate.The campaign materials showed what he had seen in Africa and connected those scenes with the products appearing in markets thousands of kilometres away.The impact of poaching reached beyond the animalsThere was also a human cost to the decline of wildlife populations. During his visit, Yao saw how tourism linked wildlife to local communities. He met schoolchildren whose education was supported by revenue associated with wildlife tourism. For conservationists, protecting elephants and rhinos was therefore tied to more than keeping animal populations alive.Poaching could undermine tourism, threaten livelihoods and make already difficult conservation work more dangerous.That point became part of Yao's public message. After seeing the consequences personally, he argued that consumers who understood how ivory and rhino horn were obtained would be less likely to purchase them.It was a shift in emphasis. Rather than treating poaching as something that happened in distant national parks, the campaign tried to make the connection between a purchase and the killing of an animal easier to understand.A visit to Nairobi brought the campaign closer to homeDuring the filming of the documentary project, Yao also visited the Nairobi Nursery run by the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust, where he met orphaned elephants and the people caring for them.Among them was Kinango, a calf only around two weeks old at the time. The encounter gave him another view of the same crisis. A young elephant was being cared for after losing its family, while only days earlier Yao had seen the bodies of elephants killed for their tusks.The two experiences were not presented as separate conservation stories. They were part of the same reality.The nursery showed what happened after elephants became victims of the ivory trade, while the carcasses he had seen in the field showed what happened before there was an orphan left to rescue.Conservation groups wanted more than awarenessThe campaign was also intended to strengthen pressure for action against the illegal trade.The African Wildlife Foundation was working in important rhino landscapes through measures including aerial surveillance, rapid-response teams and additional personnel on the ground. Its position was that poaching, rather than habitat loss alone, had become a major immediate threat to African rhinos because of demand for their horns in Asian markets.WildAid, meanwhile, pointed to previous instances in which illegal markets had been weakened through a combination of clear laws, enforcement and consumer awareness.The argument was that enforcement could address the people supplying wildlife products, but reducing demand required consumers to understand what their purchases represented.Yao Ming turned his fame into a message against wildlife crimeYao had spent much of his career as a sporting celebrity. He was one of China's most recognisable athletes, and his years in the NBA had made him familiar to audiences well beyond the country.The conservation campaign used that recognition for a subject far removed from sport.Instead of appearing in an advertisement for a commercial product, Yao was asking people not to buy something. His own experience in Africa supplied the central evidence for the message: he had seen living elephants, then seen what happened to others that had been killed for ivory.The wider lesson was about demandThe campaign's underlying idea was relatively simple. Poaching in Africa and consumption in Asia were connected parts of the same trade.Stopping the killing therefore required action at both ends. In Africa, conservation organisations and authorities had to protect animals, investigate poaching and intercept illegal shipments. In consumer markets, people had to understand that ivory and rhino horn were not harmless luxury goods detached from their origins.The surveys suggested that public attitudes could move in that direction. Large majorities of respondents supported stronger government action, even though many did not fully understand how the products reached consumers.Yao Ming turned his fame into a platform for conservationThe campaign marked a notable change in the public role Yao Ming was taking after basketball.His sporting career had given him an enormous audience. The conservation work gave that audience a different subject to consider. His Africa trip allowed him to bring images and first-hand observations from the field back to Chinese viewers who might otherwise have encountered the ivory and rhino horn trade only as consumer goods. The organisations behind the campaign hoped that familiarity could translate into influence.Yao himself framed the issue around what he had witnessed. After seeing poached elephants and a rhino, he said he could not see the products in the same way.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy Trial: Juror dispute deepens as judge rejects removal request
articles.summary: US News: A six-day deadlock in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial intensified on Thursday after Judge William Sullivan refused a defence request to remove a juror.
articles.body: A six-day deadlock in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial intensified on Thursday after Judge William Sullivan refused a defence request to remove a juror accused of failing to follow his instructions on reasonable doubt.The Massachusetts case has drawn widespread attention over the deaths of Clancy's three young children, as her defence claims that postpartum psychosis left her unable to understand the wrongfulness of her actions when the children were killed.The jury of nine women and three men had deliberated for about 35 hours and twice told Sullivan it could not reach a verdict before the dispute over the individual juror emerged. The central question before the panel is whether Clancy was criminally responsible for the killings.Judge refuses to remove disputed jurorBefore ruling on the defence request, Sullivan questioned jurors individually and again instructed the panel on the legal standard of reasonable doubt.Explaining his decision, Sullivan said the court should not choose between competing positions inside the deliberation room.“I don't feel it is proper for me to side with one side or the other of the deliberations,” Sullivan said.He also said it was not for him to determine which position within the jury was correct, noting that jurors had sworn to follow the court's instructions.Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague backed Sullivan's approach, arguing that the court should not attempt to decide which side of the disagreement was right. A conviction requires a unanimous verdict based on proof beyond a reasonable doubt, with prosecutors carrying the burden of establishing guilt.Clancy's lawyer, Kevin Reddington, said the dispute began with a note from the jury foreperson indicating that one juror was refusing to follow Sullivan's instruction on reasonable doubt.Sullivan did not disclose the wording of the note in open court. Reddington later described its contents, according to the BBC.The latest communication differed from the jury's earlier notes, which said the panel remained divided but did not accuse an individual juror of disregarding the judge's instructions.Jury reported two earlier impassesJurors first told Sullivan on Tuesday that they had been unable to reach an agreement. He asked them to continue deliberating, citing the volume of evidence presented during the nearly six-week trial, which included more than 80 witnesses and more than 300 exhibits.The jury returned on Wednesday with another note saying it remained divided.Sullivan then gave a Tuey-Rodriguez instruction, a Massachusetts charge used when jurors report difficulty reaching a unanimous decision. It asks jurors to reconsider opposing views without abandoning an honestly held judgment merely to reach a verdict.By Thursday, the issue had shifted from whether the jury needed more time to whether the reported conduct of one juror justified removal from the panel.Reddington later described the disagreement more sharply, saying “there's one juror who refuses to listen to the law that you've given him or her on reasonable doubt."Jury weighs Clancy's criminal responsibilityClancy, 36, faces three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her children — Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months — at the family's home in Duxbury, Massachusetts, on January 24, 2023.The former labour and delivery nurse does not dispute that she strangled the three children in the basement of the house. The issue before jurors is whether she was criminally responsible at the time.Her defence says Clancy was suffering from postpartum psychosis and could not understand the wrongfulness of her actions.Prosecutors accept that Clancy had mental-health problems but argue that they did not prevent her from understanding that killing her children was wrong.Clancy later jumped from a second-floor window and was left paralysed from the waist down. Experts called by the prosecution and defence disagreed over her mental state and whether she could recognise that her actions were wrong.Jurors may convict Clancy of first-degree murder, second-degree murder or manslaughter if they find her criminally responsible. They may also acquit her or find her not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility.A first-degree murder conviction carries life imprisonment without the possibility of parole.If found not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility, Clancy could be sent to a state psychiatric facility for evaluation and potentially remain committed if a court finds that the legal requirements for continued confinement are met.Mistrial remains possibleIf the jury again reports that it cannot reach a verdict, Sullivan could order further deliberations or declare a mistrial.If the trial ends without a verdict, prosecutors could seek a new trial, drop the charges or pursue a negotiated resolution.Plymouth County District Attorney Timothy Cruz declined on Thursday to say whether prosecutors would retry Clancy if the case ends without a verdict.The 12-member jury is due to return on Friday for a seventh day of deliberations. Reddington said Sullivan was also expected to question the disputed juror again.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Outstanding achievement': PM Modi hails Isro after successful EOS-05 launch
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday lauded the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) after the successful launch of the GSLV-F17 roc.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday lauded the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) after the successful launch of the GSLV-F17 rocket carrying the advanced Earth Observation Satellite-05 (EOS-05), calling the mission an “outstanding achievement” and a proud moment for the nation.The satellite was launched by Isro from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on Friday aboard the GSLV-F17. The rocket precisely placed the 2,367-kg EOS-05 into its intended sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit (Sub-GTO), marking another major milestone for India’s space programme.“Yet another outstanding achievement by ISRO and a proud moment for our nation. The successful launch of GSLV-F17 carrying EOS-05, India’s first-ever imaging satellite from Geosynchronous orbit is a reflection of the excellence, innovation and growing capabilities that define India’s space sector," PM Modi said in a post on X.The Prime Minister also highlighted the expanding role of Indian industry in the country's space programme. He said the growing partnership with ISRO was helping strengthen the sector and broaden India's capabilities."The growing partnership between ISRO and Indian industry is adding new strength and scale to our space programme and expanding India’s capabilities across the entire space ecosystem," he added.Isro chief V Narayanan described the mission as a significant achievement for India's space programme. He said the satellite was in good health after being injected into orbit.“I am very happy to announce that the GSLV-F17 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the Advanced Earth Observation Satellite 05, the geo-imaging satellite, in the intended and required orbit," he said.Narayanan said EOS-05 would become India's first dedicated imaging satellite operating from a geosynchronous orbit once it is operationalised. The satellite is expected to provide important strategic data for the country.“Today, we have injected the heaviest satellite, 2367 kgs, using this launch vehicle. The health of the satellite is perfectly alright,” the ISRO chief said.The GSLV-F17 mission was the 19th flight of India's geosynchronous satellite launch vehicle. It was launched from the second launch pad at Sriharikota and carried EOS-05 towards a sub-GTO.The mission adds to India's growing earth observation capabilities while highlighting the increasing technological strength of its space programme.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2020, Salesforce founder Marc Benioff backed a global effort to conserve and restore 1 trillion trees, later expanding his climate giving to $300 million
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In 2020, Marc and Lynne Benioff put their support behind one of the world's most ambitious forest-restoration efforts: the goal of conserving, restori.
articles.body: In 2020, Marc and Lynne Benioff put their support behind one of the world's most ambitious forest-restoration efforts: the goal of conserving, restoring and growing 1 trillion trees by the end of the decade. The Benioffs provided the initial financial support to establish 1t.org, a global movement dedicated to accelerating forest conservation and restoration. But their environmental giving soon expanded far beyond that original commitment. In October 2021, the Benioffs and Salesforce announced $300 million in investments aimed at ecosystem restoration and climate justice. According to Salesforce's official announcement, this included a new $100 million Benioff TIME Tree Fund, another $100 million investment through TIME Ventures in ecopreneurs and reforestation ventures, and $100 million in Salesforce grants over the following decade. By then, the Benioffs had already provided $68 million in climate-related grants since 2016. Their environmental philanthropy also extended to ocean conservation, climate technology and community-based forest management, making the trillion-tree campaign part of a much broader climate strategy.Marc Benioff helped launch the global 1 trillion trees effortThe Benioffs' involvement with the trillion-tree movement began in January 2020, when they provided the initial financial support to establish 1t.org. The global movement set out to conserve, restore and grow one trillion trees by the end of the decade, linking governments, businesses, communities and conservation organisations around forest protection. Salesforce's 2021 announcement explained that the initiative was intended to help sequester carbon while restoring and conserving ecosystems. By October 2021, Salesforce had already funded more than 40 million trees towards its own 100-million-tree goal. The company was also a founding member of 1t.org and had made ecosystem restoration one of the central pillars of its climate strategy. The Benioffs' early financial backing therefore helped establish a platform that treated forests as an important part of the global response to climate change rather than focusing solely on corporate emissions reductions.The Benioff TIME Tree Fund added $100 million for forest restorationIn October 2021, Marc and Lynne Benioff announced the $100 million Benioff TIME Tree Fund, designed to accelerate global reforestation efforts associated with 1t.org. According to Salesforce's official announcement, the fund would focus particularly on indigenous and community-based forest management and on helping vulnerable communities and natural ecosystems in emerging and developing countries cope with climate change. The fund formed part of a larger $200 million package of new climate investments from the Benioffs, $100 million for the tree fund and another $100 million through TIME Ventures for ecopreneurs and reforestation ventures. Salesforce reported that the Benioffs had already provided $68 million in climate-related grants since 2016, showing that the 2021 announcement was an expansion of an existing environmental giving programme rather than the beginning of their climate philanthropy.Marc Benioff’s wider environmental giving reached $300 million in 2021The tree fund was only one part of the $300 million environmental package announced by the Benioffs and Salesforce in 2021. Alongside the $200 million in new Benioff climate investments, Salesforce committed another $100 million in grants over 10 years for non-profit organisations working on ecosystem restoration and climate justice. The company also pledged to donate technology and enable its employees to provide 2.5 million volunteer hours to organisations focused on climate action. TIME Ventures was simultaneously committing $100 million to ecopreneurs, building on another $100 million the Benioffs said they had already invested in climate-focused entrepreneurs since 2014. The announcement showed how their environmental giving had developed into several interconnected areas: restoring ecosystems, supporting new climate technologies, helping communities and financing organisations working on climate action.His environmental philanthropy also extended from forests to oceansThe Benioffs' environmental commitments have not been limited to trees. Salesforce's 2021 announcement noted that in 2016 they donated $10 million to the University of California, Santa Barbara, and founded the Benioff Ocean Initiative, a science-based organisation focused on developing ocean solutions. The initiative had funded projects involving technologies designed to intercept plastic in rivers before it reaches the sea, as well as Whale Safe, an AI-powered whale-detection system intended to help ships avoid collisions with whales. The Benioffs also partnered with the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation and NOAA on the Pacific Islands Research and Conservation programme and became founding members of the World Economic Forum's Friends of Ocean Action initiative, providing nearly $11 million through the Benioff Ocean Initiative. Their environmental giving consequently spans forests, oceans, climate technology and ecosystem restoration, with the trillion-tree campaign forming one of the most visible pieces of a much larger effort to address climate change and nature loss.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nepal estimates $2.56 billion flood damage, faces $52.6 million recovery cost
articles.summary: South Asia News: Nepal has estimated that the devastating floods that hit the country last week caused at least $2.56 billion in damage to property, housing and infras.
articles.body: Nepal has estimated that the devastating floods that hit the country last week caused at least $2.56 billion in damage to property, housing and infrastructure. The government also expects to spend another $52.6 million on early recovery, officials said on Friday.The damage estimate, equivalent to 387.5 billion Nepalese rupees, covers homes, roads and other critical infrastructure destroyed or damaged in the floods. The initial recovery cost of 7.95 billion rupees will cover work over the first four months, including rebuilding roads, setting up temporary shelters and restoring drinking water and electricity.The scale of the destruction has left thousands displaced and added pressure on rescue and relief operations.Thousands remain displacedMore than 4,500 people displaced by the floods are currently living in 38 relief centres across Nepal.For many survivors, however, basic needs remain difficult to meet. People in some camps have struggled to obtain essential medicines and cash, even as authorities distribute food and other relief supplies.Suresh Kumar Karanjit, who is staying at a relief centre in Devighat in badly affected Nuwakot district, lost his younger brother in the floods. He said the centre did not have the medicine prescribed for his heart condition.Karanjit eventually raised money for his regular medicine by selling a carton of noodles he had received as relief for 400 rupees, or about $2.60.“We have been living here for a week. The relief materials are being provided, which is good. But there is a lack of medicine,” he said.Nepal's disaster authority chief Dharma Raj Uprety said health centres staffed by doctors and stocked with medicines had been established at each shelter. Authorities were also prioritising hygiene and sanitation to limit the spread of disease.Roads and bridges destroyedThe Aug. 26 floods devastated towns and valleys across Nepal, destroying homes, roads, bridges and other vital infrastructure.The floods were likely triggered by a glacier collapse, according to authorities.At least 1,259 people have been killed and more than 5,000 remain missing, Nepal's disaster management agency said. On the Tibet side of the border, China said 21 people had been killed and 541 remained missing as of late Wednesday.The destruction has also cut off several communities from normal transport routes.In Bidur, a town along the Trishuli River, residents have been using a temporary zip line to cross the river. Army personnel have been helping people use the makeshift crossing and assisting them on the opposite bank.Rescue teams search hydroelectric tunnelsIn a long-awaited breakthrough, two workers were also rescued from the Trishula 3A hydropower tunnel. Nepal's energy minister shared the updates on the workers trapped for nine days. Workers have begun manually opening the upper section of the passage, according to lawmaker Ram Neupane.An access road was constructed over the past week to reach the excavation site. But rescuers still face major obstacles. More rock blasting and debris removal will be required before heavy machinery can be brought to the area.Rescue operations have also shifted towards several hydroelectric projects where workers are believed to be trapped inside tunnels.About 900 workers remain missing. Specialised rescue teams from India, China and the United States are taking part in efforts to reach them.Recovery effort beginsThe government's early recovery estimate highlights the immediate financial burden created by the disaster.Upreti said the projected $52.6 million would be needed during the first four months to restore essential services and provide temporary support to affected communities.The longer-term cost is expected to be far higher, given the scale of damage to housing, roads and infrastructure and the continuing search for missing people.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Two trapped workers rescued alive from a tunnel in Nepal
articles.summary: Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a tunnel Friday during an ongoing operation at the Trishul 3A tunnel, officials said.
articles.body: KATHMANDU, Nepal — Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a tunnel Friday during an ongoing operation at the Trishul 3A tunnel, officials said. Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane posted about the second rescue on his Facebook page shortly after army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet confirmed the first trapped worker’s rescue during the operation at the tunnel. Officials identified the two men as a mechanical foreman and a mechanical supervisor. The rescues come nine days after the Aug. 26 floods, likely caused by a glacier collapse, that devastated towns and valleys in Nepal. Local television news channels showed images of the first rescued worker covered in mud and being carried from the site on a rescuer’s shoulder. Both men were under medical observation, the officials said. At least 557 workers are missing from the Trishuli 3A hydropower project along the Trishuli River, with about 115 believed to be trapped in the main tunnel, according to the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal. Officials present at the rescue site said rescuers believe some people may still be alive inside the tunnel. At least 1,259 people were killed and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to the country’s disaster management agency. China, as of late Wednesday, said 21 people were killed and 541 were missing on the Tibet side of the border. About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects in Nepal, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels, according to local authorities.
